goal: Make -networkactive=0 actually stop NAT-PMP and Tor control activity, not just at startup
Fixes a documented mismatch where the flag was ignored by these subsystems, benefiting privacy-conscious operators
reviewability: Stale: needs rebase and author has been silent for about 30 days since last force-push
An open backoff-reset edge case from winterrdog is unaddressed but was raised alongside an approach ACK, so it's not itself blocking
agreement: Broadly positive with several concept, tested, and approach ACKs (sedited, fanquake, Jhackman2019, bradleystachurski, brunoerg, winterrdog)
Verified by independent Docker-based testing showing traffic stops and resumes correctly (brunoerg)
Nonblocking objection: backoff timer may not reset on rapid networkactive toggling during Tor reconnect sleep, no author reply yet (winterrdog)
A prior nit about resetting reconnect_timeout was implemented by the author (bradleystachurski)

categories.name: p2p
why: P2 because it fixes a real mismatch between the networkactive=0 flag and actual NAT-PMP/Tor behavior
Benefits any operator relying on the flag to fully suspend outbound network activity, including Tor users
Independently verified via packet capture that traffic actually stops and resumes with the fix
